items.stem: What is meant by “mole fraction”?
items.answer: The ratio of the number of moles of one component to the total number of moles of all components.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the ratio of the number of moles of one component to the total number of moles of all components.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as liquid solution or solid solution: oxygen dissolved in water, copper dissolved in gold, ethanol dissolved in water, amalgam of mercury with sodium.
items.answer: oxygen dissolved in water – liquid solution; copper dissolved in gold – solid solution; ethanol dissolved in water – liquid solution; amalgam of mercury with sodium – solid solution.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: oxygen dissolved in water – liquid solution; copper dissolved in gold – solid solution; ethanol dissolved in water – liquid solution; amalgam of mercury with sodium – solid solution.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a liquid solution?
items.answer: chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas
items.markingKey: (b) Chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas is a gaseous solution, not a liquid solution.
options: ethanol dissolved in water
chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas
glucose dissolved in water
oxygen dissolved in water

items.stem: A 1000 kg sample of water is found to contain 20 g of a substance (fluoride in drinking water). Express its concentration in parts per million (ppm) by mass.
items.answer: 20.0 ppm
items.markingKey: ppm = mass of component / total mass × 10⁶ = 20 g / 1000000 g × 10⁶ = 20.0 ppm.

items.stem: A solution is made by mixing 46 g of ethanol (C₂H₅OH) with 36 g of water. Calculate the mole fraction of the solute. (Molar mass of solute = 46 g mol⁻¹, water = 18 g mol⁻¹)
items.markingKey: n(solute) = 1 mol, n(water) = 2 mol; x = 1/(1 + 2) = 0.333.

items.stem: Concentrated nitric acid used in the laboratory is 68% HNO₃ by mass. What other information is needed to express this as molarity, and why?
items.answer: The density of the solution; molarity needs the volume of solution, which is obtained from mass and density (V = m/d).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: density; 1 mark: molarity needs volume of solution.

items.stem: A commercial sample of NH₃ is 28% by mass and has a density of 0.9 g mL⁻¹. Calculate its molarity. (Molar mass = 17 g mol⁻¹)
10 g of copper sulphate is dissolved in 200 g of water. What is the mass percentage of copper sulphate in the solution?
items.markingKey: Mass % = mass of solute / mass of solution × 100 = 10/(10 + 200) × 100 = 4.76%.

items.stem: Calculate the molality of a solution containing 6 g of NaCl in 200 g of water. (Molar mass = 58.5 g mol⁻¹)
items.answer: 0.513 mol kg⁻¹
items.markingKey: n = 6/58.5 = 0.103 mol; m = n / mass of solvent (kg) = 0.103/0.2 = 0.513 mol kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Which of the following is a gaseous solution?
items.answer: a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen gases
items.markingKey: (c) A mixture of oxygen and nitrogen gases is a gaseous solution; the others are not.
options: glucose dissolved in water
oxygen dissolved in water
a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen gases
amalgam of mercury with sodium

items.stem: What is meant by “a binary solution”?
items.answer: A solution containing two components.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a solution containing two components.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In a gaseous solution the solvent is a liquid.”
items.answer: In a gaseous solution the solvent is a gas.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: In a gaseous solution the solvent is a gas.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Brass is a solid solution of zinc in copper.
Reason (R): Mole fraction of a component can be greater than one.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Mole fraction is always less than one; all mole fractions add up to 1.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Aarav dissolves 14.9 g of KCl in water and makes the solution up to 1000 mL in a volumetric flask. Calculate the molarity. (Molar mass = 74.5 g mol⁻¹)
Explain the term “the bends”.
items.answer: A painful condition in deep-sea divers caused by nitrogen bubbles forming in the blood on rapid ascent.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a painful condition in deep-sea divers caused by nitrogen bubbles forming in the blood on rapid ascent.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about solubility and Henry's law is correct?
items.answer: Scuba divers use air diluted with helium to reduce the bends.
items.markingKey: (d) Scuba divers use air diluted with helium to reduce the bends. The other statements are false. x = p/K_H, so higher K_H means lower solubility. Solids and liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure has little effect. Cold water holds more dissolved oxygen, so aquatic life is more comfortable in cold water.
options: Pressure greatly increases the solubility of solids in liquids.
Aquatic species are more comfortable in warm water.
A higher K_H value means higher solubility of the gas.
Scuba divers use air diluted with helium to reduce the bends.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Pressure has no significant effect on the solubility of solids in liquids.
Reason (R): Pressure greatly increases the solubility of solids in liquids.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Solids and liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure has little effect.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Read the situation: gas dissolution is exothermic; fish survive better in cold water; more oxygen dissolves at lower temperature. Which application or effect of gas solubility is illustrated? Give a reason.
items.answer: Aquatic life in cold water
items.markingKey: 1 mark: aquatic life in cold water; 1 mark: the features gas dissolution is exothermic; fish survive better in cold water; more oxygen dissolves at lower temperature are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Soft drink bottles are sealed under high pressure.
Reason (R): The solubility of CO₂ in water increases with its partial pressure.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Henry's law.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the situation: on rapid ascent nitrogen comes out of the blood as bubbles; divers breathe air under high pressure deep under water.
(i) Which application or effect of gas solubility is illustrated? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were aquatic life in cold water? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The bends in scuba divers (ii) tanks are diluted with helium to avoid it (iii) gas dissolution is exothermic; more oxygen dissolves at lower temperature
items.markingKey: (i) the bends in scuba divers – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: tanks are diluted with helium to avoid it – 1 mark. (iii) for aquatic life in cold water: fish survive better in cold water; more oxygen dissolves at lower temperature; gas dissolution is exothermic – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: At 298 K the Henry's law constants of O₂ and Ar in water are 34.86 kbar and 40.3 kbar. Which gas is more soluble in water at the same partial pressure?
items.answer: O₂
items.markingKey: (a) x = p/K_H, so the gas with the smaller K_H (O₂) has the higher solubility.
options: O₂
both are equally soluble
cannot be predicted from K_H
Ar

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The solubility of gases in water increases with temperature.”
items.answer: Gas solubility decreases with rise in temperature because dissolution is exothermic.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Gas solubility decreases with rise in temperature because dissolution is exothermic.

items.stem: Give two differences between the bends in scuba divers and aquatic life in cold water.
items.answer: The bends in scuba divers: tanks are diluted with helium to avoid it; divers breathe air under high pressure deep under water. Aquatic life in cold water: more oxygen dissolves at lower temperature; gas dissolution is exothermic.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the bends in scuba divers – tanks are diluted with helium to avoid it; divers breathe air under high pressure deep under water; aquatic life in cold water – more oxygen dissolves at lower temperature; gas dissolution is exothermic.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about solubility and Henry's law is incorrect?
items.answer: Pressure greatly increases the solubility of solids in liquids.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Pressure greatly increases the solubility of solids in liquids.” Correct form: Solids and liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure has little effect.
options: The solubility of a gas in a liquid decreases with increase in temperature.
A higher value of K_H means a lower solubility of the gas.
Pressure greatly increases the solubility of solids in liquids.
Dissolution of a gas in a liquid is generally exothermic.

items.stem: Why do climbers at high altitudes, such as on the way to Ladakh, often feel weak and unable to think clearly?
items.answer: At high altitude the partial pressure of oxygen is low; by Henry's law less oxygen dissolves in the blood (anoxia).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: low partial pressure of O₂; 1 mark: Henry's law ⇒ low dissolved O₂.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Pressure greatly increases the solubility of solids in liquids.”
items.answer: Solids and liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure has little effect.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Solids and liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure has little effect.

items.stem: What is meant by “a minimum boiling azeotrope”?
items.answer: An azeotrope formed by solutions showing large positive deviation from Raoult's law.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an azeotrope formed by solutions showing large positive deviation from Raoult's law.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about vapour pressure and Raoult's law is correct?
items.answer: Chloroform and acetone form hydrogen bonds on mixing.
items.markingKey: (b) Chloroform and acetone form hydrogen bonds on mixing. The other statements are false. It shows negative deviation because new hydrogen bonds form between them. Azeotropes boil at constant composition, so they cannot be separated by fractional distillation. Ethanol–water shows positive deviation (H-bonds in ethanol are broken).
options: Azeotropes can be separated by fractional distillation.
Chloroform and acetone form hydrogen bonds on mixing.
A mixture of chloroform and acetone shows positive deviation.
Ethanol and water show negative deviation from Raoult's law.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Ethanol and water show negative deviation from Raoult's law.
Reason (R): An ideal solution has ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Ethanol–water shows positive deviation (H-bonds in ethanol are broken). R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.answer: Azeotropes boil at constant composition, so they cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Azeotropes boil at constant composition, so they cannot be separated by fractional distillation.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem:
A binary liquid mixture shows: ΔmixH negative (heat evolved on mixing); ΔmixV negative (volume decreases); forms maximum boiling azeotrope at a certain composition.

(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were a solution with positive deviation? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) A solution with negative deviation (ii) A–B interactions stronger than A–A and B–B (iii) forms minimum boiling azeotrope at a certain composition; ΔmixV positive (volume increases)
items.markingKey: (i) a solution with negative deviation – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: A–B interactions stronger than A–A and B–B – 1 mark. (iii) for a solution with positive deviation: A–B interactions weaker than A–A and B–B; ΔmixH positive (heat absorbed on mixing); ΔmixV positive (volume increases) – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: When 50 mL of ethanol is mixed with 50 mL of water the volume of the solution is slightly less than 100 mL, yet the mixture shows positive deviation in vapour pressure. Discuss what each observation tells you.
items.answer: Volume contraction shows strong ethanol–water H-bonding and close packing; positive deviation in vapour pressure arises because ethanol–ethanol H-bonds are broken and the escaping tendency increases. Real solutions are more complex than the simple model.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: interpretation of volume; 1 mark: interpretation of vapour pressure.

items.answer: bromoethane + chloroethane

items.answer: A solution with negative deviation
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a solution with negative deviation; 1 mark: the features ΔmixV negative (volume decreases); forms maximum boiling azeotrope at a certain composition are characteristic of it.

items.stem: What is meant by “a maximum boiling azeotrope”?
items.answer: An azeotrope formed by solutions showing large negative deviation from Raoult's law.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an azeotrope formed by solutions showing large negative deviation from Raoult's law.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a solution with negative deviation and an ideal solution on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A binary liquid mixture shows: ΔmixH = 0. What type of solution is it – a solution with negative deviation or an ideal solution? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A solution with negative deviation: A–B interactions stronger than A–A and B–B; ΔmixH negative (heat evolved on mixing); ΔmixV negative (volume decreases). An ideal solution: A–B interactions nearly equal to A–A and B–B; ΔmixH = 0; ΔmixV = 0. (b) An ideal solution.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: an ideal solution; 1 mark: “ΔmixH = 0” is a feature of an ideal solution.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law or nearly ideal solution: n-hexane + n-heptane, phenol + aniline, hydrochloric acid + water, nitric acid + water.
items.answer: n-hexane + n-heptane – nearly ideal solution; phenol + aniline – solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law; hydrochloric acid + water – solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law; nitric acid + water – solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: n-hexane + n-heptane – nearly ideal solution; phenol + aniline – solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law; hydrochloric acid + water – solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law; nitric acid + water – solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law.

items.answer: The ratio of the normal molar mass to the abnormal (observed) molar mass of a solute.

items.stem:
Read and answer. People living in hilly regions of Himachal Pradesh add ethylene glycol to car radiators in winter. In coastal cities, reverse osmosis plants supply drinking water.
(i) Which colligative property is used in the first case? (1 mark)
(ii) Why is reverse osmosis called "reverse"? (1 mark)
(iii) Calculate the mass of ethylene glycol (62 g mol⁻¹) needed per kg of water to lower its freezing point by 6 K. (K_f = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹) (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Depression of freezing point. (ii) Pressure greater than the osmotic pressure forces solvent from solution to solvent side, opposite to osmosis. (iii) m = 6/1.86 = 3.23 mol kg⁻¹; mass = 3.23 × 62 = 200 g.

items.stem: Why does a raw mango placed in concentrated salt solution shrivel, while a dried raisin placed in water swells?
